==English== {{wp|[[business|+]]}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/fɜːm/|a=RP,AU}} ** {{audio|en|en-uk-firm.ogg|a=UK}} ** {{audio|en|EN-AU ck1 firm.ogg|a=AU}} * {{IPA|en|/fɜɹm/|[fɚm]|a=GenAm}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-firm.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/fɪɾm/|a=Scotland}} * {{IPA|en|/føːm/|a=NZ,Wales}} * {{IPA|en|/feːm/|a=Scouse,square-nurse}} * {{IPA|en|/fɛːm/|a=Humberside,Teesside,square-nurse}} * {{rhymes|en|ɜː(ɹ)m|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰer-}} {{etymon|en|id=business|:bor|it:firma|tree=1}} From {{bor|en|it|firma||signature}}, from {{m|it|firmare||to sign}}, from {{der|en|la|firmāre||to make firm, to confirm (by signature)}}, from {{m|la|firmus||firm, stable}}. The contemporary sense developed in the 18th century simultaneously with {{der|en|de|Firma||business, name of business}}. There are conflicting statements in the literature as to which of the two languages influenced which. {{doublet|en|dharma|dhamma}}. Other cognates include {{cog|ru|держать||to hold}}. ====Noun==== {{en-noun}} # {{lb|en|UK|business}} A [[business]] [[partnership]]; the name under which it [[trade]]s. # {{lb|en|business|economics}} A business [[enterprise]], however organized. #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:enterprise}} #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-06-01|volume=407|issue=8838|page=71 |title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21578670-peer-peer-lending-needs-new-name-end-peer-show End of the peer show] |passage=Finance is seldom romantic. But the idea of peer-to-peer lending comes close. This is an industry that brings together individual savers and lenders on online platforms.{{...}}Banks and credit-card '''firms''' are kept out of the picture. Talk to enough people in the field and someone is bound to mention the “democratisation of finance”.}} # {{lb|en|slang}} A [[criminal]] [[gang]], especially based around [[football hooliganism]]. Wedeck}}|title=Dictionary of Aphrodisiacs|publisher=The Citadel Press|location=New York|page=219|passage=Biblical criteria of sexual seductiveness include a white skin, black hair, or henna-dyed, scarlet lips, a prominent nose, rosy temples, long straight neck, '''firm''' breasts, round thighs, an erect posture.}} # [[mentally|Mentally]] [[resistant]] to [[hurt]] or [[stress]]. #* {{RQ:Tennyson In Memoriam|XVIII|30|[…] The life that almost dies in me:
That dies not, but endures with pain,
⁠And slowly forms the '''firmer''' mind,
⁠Treasuring the look it cannot find,
The words that are not heard again.}} # Not [[frivolous]] or [[fallacious]]; [[trustworthy]]; [[solid]]; [[dependable]]. =====Synonyms===== {{col|en|decided|}} =====Derived terms===== {{col3|en|firm error |firm hand |firm hand at the tiller |firm hand on the tiller |firmhearted |firmish |firm line |firm link |firmly |firmness |firm power |firm up |firmware |hold firm |semifirm |stand firm |unfirm |windfirm }} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|steadfast, secure (position)}} * Arabic: * Armenian: * Azerbaijani: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Finnish: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Gothic: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hindi: * Hungarian: * Indonesian: * Irish: * Latgalian: * Latin: * Latvian: * Māori: * Middle English: * Plautdietsch: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|кре́пкий}}, {{t+|ru|твёрдый}}, {{t+|ru|про́чный}}, {{t+|ru|усто́йчивый}} * Sanskrit: * Scottish Gaelic: * Slovene: * Spanish: * Sundanese: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|fixed (in opinions)}} * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Chinese: * Czech: * Esperanto: * Estonian: * Finnish: * Galician: * Georgian: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hungarian: * Italian: * Latin: * Latvian: * Māori: * Middle English: * Old English: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|непоколеби́мый}}, {{t+|ru|непрекло́нный}}, {{t+|ru|реши́тельный}} * Scottish Gaelic: * Spanish: * Sundanese: * Swedish: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|solid, rigid (material state)}} * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Czech: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * Galician: * Georgian: * German: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hungarian: * Latin: * Latvian: * Māori: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Russian: {{t+|ru|твёрдый}} * Slovene: * Sorbian: * Spanish: * Swedish: * Tausug: * Ukrainian: {{trans-bottom}} {{checktrans-top}} * Norman: {{t-check|nrf|fèrme}} {{qualifier|Jersey}} {{trans-bottom}} ====Adverb==== {{en-adv}} # {{lb|en|transitive|colloquial}} To [[grit one's teeth]] and [[bear]]; to [[push through]] something unpleasant. #: {{ux|en|I know you aren't feeling well, but just '''firm''' it.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|UK|slang}} To [[select]] (a [[higher education]] [[institution]]) as one's preferred choice, so as to [[enrol]] automatically if one's [[grade]]s match the [[conditional]] [[offer]]. =====Derived terms===== * {{l|en|firming agent}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|to make firm or strong}} * Bulgarian: * Czech: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * Greek: * Hungarian: * Māori: * Middle English: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Slovene: * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to fix securely}} * Bulgarian: * Czech: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * Greek: * Hungarian: * Māori: * Portuguese: * Slovene: * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to solidify}} * Bulgarian: * Czech: * Finnish: * Greek: * Hungarian: * Māori: * Slovene: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to become firm}} * Bulgarian: * Czech: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * Greek: * Hungarian: * Polish: * Spanish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|to improve after decline}} * Finnish: * Greek: * Hungarian: {{trans-bottom}} ===References=== {{reflist}} ===Further reading=== {{R:Britannica 1911|Firm}} ===Anagrams=== * {{anagrams|en|a=fimr|FRIM|fMRI|frim}} {{C|en|Collectives}}
